+**External Heat Block Override** keeps the plan from holding back while

@@ -1,3 +1,88 @@
+## v10.1.7
+
+**Patch stamp: 2 merges since v10.1.6 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v10.1.6..HEAD | wc -l`): state that production stored and never read is deleted, with no behaviour change, and the round-11 mutant kills are recorded in the mutation ledger.**
+
+### Action needed
+
+Nothing asks you to act: no entity id of an existing install changes and no option default changes.
+
+### #3931 Unread state deleted (R11-SEAM-dead-state)
+
+Imports, parameters, locals and stored fields that no production code reads are removed from the modules that held them and from their callers. The integration behaves as before.
+
+### Tooling, tests and CI
+
+- #3938: the mutant kills the round-11 test-gap finders measured are pinned in the mutation ledger, so later rounds do not screen them again.
+
+## v10.1.6
+
+**Patch stamp: 13 merges since v10.1.5 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v10.1.5..HEAD | wc -l`): a stored option of the wrong type now reads as its default instead of raising, a stored boolean in the persisted store reads as absent where a number is declared, and the rest is test pins, review and CI tooling.**
+
+### Action needed
+
+Nothing asks you to act: no entity id of an existing install changes and no option default changes.
+
+### #3913 Stored options of the wrong type read as their default (R11-LATE-P1-OPTIONS)
+
+A configuration option stored as something other than a number (for example an empty string left by an older version) no longer raises out of the readers that convert it; each reader treats it as unset and uses its default, as it does for a missing option.
+
+### #3932 Stored booleans read as absent at the store's load boundary (R11-SEAM-store part 2)
+
+When the persisted store holds `true` or `false` where a number is declared, loading now treats the value as absent instead of reading it as 1 or 0. Follows part 1, #3875.
+
+### Tooling, tests and CI
+
+- #3928, #3927: tests-only pins for the plant-model and money seams' mutants the full gate did not kill.
+- #3936: review verdicts carry automatically to a head whose own diff is unchanged.
+- #3935, #3929, #3926, #3923: CI queue changes from #3885 (a run that would wait on another run's sources defers at once; scheduling and cancellation steps).
+- #3937: the D6 claim register merges row by row by claim id.
+- #3924: the instrument self-tests run in shards.
+- #3912, #3911: flow-metrics replay timeout and merge counts.
+
+## v10.1.5
+
+**Patch stamp: 24 merges since v10.1.4 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v10.1.4..HEAD | wc -l`): set-point writes stay inside the range the entity accepts, with an optional manual high limit; a switch lets the plan run while external heat is detected; a hot-water run the pump would not start is no longer kept on the first step; a two-zone valve-fed slab is priced in the flow set; the room lift is named in the plan and narrative; one predicate decides which intervals the learners may ingest; the rest is entity metadata, refactors, tooling, CI, audit records and the round-11 roster.**
+
+### Action needed
+
+Nothing asks you to act: no entity id of an existing install changes and no option default changes. Changes you may notice without acting: a new optional option, `space_setpoint_high_limit_c` (entities page, indoor group, shown for a water set-point only), caps the space flow set-point where the pump advertises no limit (#3866); a new switch, External Heat Block Override, lets the plan run while external heat is detected (#3874); plan steps held up by the room lift now read `room_floor`, with a `room_lift` driver row (#3838); the system-identification and diagnose buttons now report why nothing ran (#3841).
+
+### #3866 Set-point writes clamped to the entity range; manual high flow limit (R11-OWNER-FLOWCAP)
+
+Every set-point write is clamped to the minimum and maximum the target entity states, rounded onto its step. The new optional option `space_setpoint_high_limit_c` (30–70 °C, no default) sets a high limit for the space water set-point; where the pump also advertises one, the lower of the two binds, and a limit below the lowest heating write is dropped and logged once.
+
+### #3874 External Heat Block Override switch (R11-OWNER-EXTHEAT-OVERRIDE)
+
+While the switch is on and external-heat detection is enabled, a detected fire no longer holds back hot water or the space plan. Detection, the External Heat Source sensor and the learning freeze keep running. Strings in en, sv and de.
+
+### #3863 A hot-water run the pump would not start is dropped (R11-OUTSIDE-3848)
+
+Reported and first fixed by outside contributor Bankaifan in #3848. On a re-plan the first step was always treated as a charge under way, so a hot-water run the pump would never start was kept and heating was locked out. The first step is now exempt only while the compressor runs in a mode serving hot water.
+
+### #3879 Two-zone valve-fed slab priced in the flow set (R11-SEAM-two-zone-slab)
+
+Behind a two-zone valve that feeds the slab, the flow set now includes the slab between the floor circuit and the lower floor, and the house's internal gains, so the curve holds the room the thermostat reads.
+
+### #3838 The room lift named in the plan (R11-OUTSIDE-ROOMS-3B)
+
+Part of #3616. Steps the room lift holds up read `room_floor`, and the why-now drivers show a `room_lift` row beside `comfort_floor`, in the card and narrative in en, sv and de. The plan itself does not change.
+
+### #3841 Entity metadata and service outcomes (R11-SEAM-entity-service)
+
+The arm and diagnose buttons raise a translated error naming why nothing ran. Three temperature-difference sensors take the temperature-delta device class on Home Assistant 2025.11 and later. The thermal-parameter service fields accept any value on their range. New installs get object ids led by their entity family; existing ids are unchanged.
+
+### #3835 One learning-freeze predicate (R11-SEAM-learners)
+
+One predicate decides which intervals each learner may ingest: away periods, unplanned charges, an open hot-water charge and a ceiling at the running floor are refused uniformly. Refs #3760, which stays open.
+
+### #3873, #3910 Refactors and replay
+
+Boost and diagnostics read the mode from their own state (#3873); the replay document drops non-finite numbers (#3910).
+
+### Tooling, CI and records
+
+#3908, #3902, #3909, #3905, #3906, #3904, #3901, #3900, #3896, #3899, #3890, #3894, #3895, #3891, #3892.
+

diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_start.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_start.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3fd2aca04f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/dhw_start.py
@@ -0,0 +1,128 @@
+"""The pump's hot-water start condition: where a planned charge is one the pump makes.
+
+A heat pump starts a hot-water charge only on a tank below its set-point less
+its start hysteresis (``thermal_model.dhw_start_below_c``). Here that rule
+becomes the per-step start temperature (:func:`dhw_start_temps`) and the
+steps a charge may be bought on (:func:`startable_steps`). It also becomes the
+floor repair that drops a charge the pump would never start and re-buys the
+floor elsewhere (:func:`drop_unstartable`, :func:`place_startable`).
+``dhw_planner.DhwPlanner`` calls them; they hold no state and read only their
+arguments.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Callable
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from .thermal_model import ThermalParameters, ThermalState, dhw_start_below_c, dhw_step_target_c
+
+
+#: How many times :func:`place_startable` re-buys what the start condition
+#: barred before it settles for dropping. A round re-buys under the charges
+#: the round before kept, and the measured placements settle in two or three
+#: (``dev/audit/harnesses/r10_dhw_start_hysteresis.py``, repair_rounds_max),
+#: so eight is that with room to spare and still a bound.
+STARTABLE_ROUNDS = 8
+
+
+def dhw_start_temps(
+    params: ThermalParameters, state: ThermalState, n_steps: int, cycle_step: int | None
+) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    """Per step, the tank temperature below which the pump starts a charge, °C.
+
+    The target the arbiter writes on that step (``dhw_step_target_c`` on the
+    set-point entity's grid, ``state.dhw_setpoint_grid``: the cycle's on
+    ``cycle_step``, the everyday one elsewhere) less the pump's start
+    hysteresis (``state.dhw_start_hysteresis_k``), so a disinfection charge
+    is judged against its own target and a stepped entity's against the step
+    it lands on. ``None`` where no start condition is known
+    (``dhw_start_below_c``).
+    """
+    hysteresis_k, grid = state.dhw_start_hysteresis_k, state.dhw_setpoint_grid
+    everyday = dhw_start_below_c(dhw_step_target_c(params, False, grid), hysteresis_k)
+    if everyday is None:
+        return None
+    start = np.full(n_steps, everyday)
+    if cycle_step is not None and 0 <= cycle_step < n_steps:
+        start[cycle_step] = dhw_start_below_c(dhw_step_target_c(params, True, grid), hysteresis_k)
+    return start
+
+
+def startable_steps(
+    plan: np.ndarray, temps: np.ndarray, start_below: np.ndarray | None, charge_running: bool = True
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The steps where charging is something the pump does.
+
+    A step that opens on a tank below its start temperature (``temps[i]``,
+    the simulated level at its start), and the step after one of a charge
+    under way, which runs on to its target. A charge is under way from the
+    step it opens below its start temperature, or from the first step when
+    ``charge_running`` (``ThermalState.dhw_charge_under_way``) says one runs
+    now. A charge the pump would not start carries nothing on, so the repair
+    buys neither inside it nor behind it. Every step where no start condition
+    is known (``start_below`` ``None``).
+    """
+    on = np.asarray(plan, dtype=float) > 0.0
+    if start_below is None:
+        return np.ones(on.size, dtype=bool)
+    ok: np.ndarray = np.asarray(temps, dtype=float)[: on.size] < start_below[: on.size]
+    under_way = bool(on[:1].any()) and (charge_running or bool(ok[:1].any()))
+    for i in range(1, on.size):
+        ok[i] |= under_way
+        under_way = bool(on[i] and ok[i])
+    return ok
+
+
+def drop_unstartable(
+    plan: np.ndarray,
+    start_below: np.ndarray,
+    temps_of: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
+    charge_running: bool = True,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """``plan`` without the charges the pump would never start.
+
+    Each run is judged in time order on the trajectory ``temps_of`` simulates
+    for the runs kept before it: one that begins on a tank at or above its
+    step's start temperature is removed whole. A run at the first step is
+    kept while ``charge_running``, a charge under way (Bankaifan, #3440); with
+    none running, it is judged like any other.
+    """
+    plan = np.array(plan, dtype=float)
+    on = plan > 0.0
+    for i in np.flatnonzero(on & ~np.append(charge_running, on[:-1])[: on.size]):
+        end = i + int(np.argmin(np.append(on[i:], False)))
+        if temps_of(plan)[i] >= start_below[i]:
+            plan[i:end] = 0.0
+    return plan
+
+
+def place_startable(
+    plan: np.ndarray,
+    start_below: np.ndarray | None,
+    temps_of: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
+    repair: Callable[..., np.ndarray],
+    charge_running: bool = True,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The floor repair of ``plan`` under the pump's start condition.
+
+    With no condition, ``repair(plan=plan)``, the call as it always was. With
+    one, the charges the pump would not start are dropped and ``repair``,
+    handed the condition so it places only on :func:`startable_steps`,
+    re-buys what the floor still needs; a top-up warms the tank under every
+    later charge, so the two repeat until the plan stands, at most
+    :data:`STARTABLE_ROUNDS` times. The plan that leaves holds no charge the
+    pump would not start, and is short of the floor only where no startable
+    step can hold it. ``charge_running`` is :func:`drop_unstartable`'s.
+    ``repair`` is not handed it: each plan it gets has been dropped first, so
+    a first-step charge in it is one the pump starts or one under way, and
+    :func:`startable_steps` reads it the same either way.
+    """
+    if start_below is None:
+        return repair(plan=plan)
+    for _ in range(STARTABLE_ROUNDS):
+        fixed = repair(plan=drop_unstartable(plan, start_below, temps_of, charge_running), start_below=start_below)
+        if np.array_equal(fixed, plan):
+            break
+        plan = fixed
+    return drop_unstartable(plan, start_below, temps_of, charge_running)

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace

+def with_dhw_under_way(state: Any, signals: PumpSignals, running: bool, action: Any) -> Any:
+    """``state`` with ``dhw_charge_under_way`` set: whether a hot-water charge runs now.
+
+    The compressor runs (``running``, ``duty_switch.running_now``) and the
+    observed mode serves hot water: hot water only, or a combined mode while
+    the executing step (``action``) plans hot water. A combined mode is what
+    the arbiter writes for a hot-water duty on a select with no hot-water
+    only option. With no mode observed a running compressor keeps the first
+    step's charge as before, and so does an unsettled or missing running
+    signal, which ``running_now`` answers from the planned draw. A pump
+    heating, or stopped, has no charge under way.
+    """
+    mode = signals.mode
+    dhw = mode.dhw and (not mode.space_heat or float(action.get("dhw_power", 0.0)) > 0.0)
+    return replace(state, dhw_charge_under_way=running and (not signals.mode_observed or dhw))
+
+

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_queue.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_queue.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..b6d7dc825c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_queue.py
@@ -0,0 +1,344 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""#3885 queue group (R11-CI-3885-QUEUE): where the account's concurrent-job slots go.
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_queue.py fetch DAY [--cache DIR]
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_queue.py report DAY [--cache DIR] [--keep-copies]
+
+`fetch` lists every workflow run created on DAY (UTC) and every job of every
+attempt of each (`/actions/runs/{id}/jobs?filter=all`), and caches both as
+JSON under DIR (default $TMPDIR/ci3885_queue). `report` reads the cache only,
+so a re-read costs no API call, and prints one JSON object, a key per arm:
+
+  census      per workflow: runs, runs that held a runner (a job with a
+              started_at and conclusion other than skipped), runner-minutes
+              (started_at..completed_at over every non-skipped job, every
+              attempt), and the day's peak concurrent jobs (the cap as seen).
+  queue       per job: started_at - created_at, p50/p90/max, all jobs and
+              by hour; and for CI runs, run created -> first job started.
+  e2e         CI runs whose latest `gate` concluded: created -> gate completed.
+  sweep       Gate sweep runs: how many held a runner, their minutes and queue
+              wait; the triggering CI attempt is not on the run object, so a
+              sweep is attributed to the CI run that completed at its head
+              closest before it (same head_sha).
+  supersede   CI pull_request/dispatch runs on a branch: minutes their jobs ran
+              after a NEWER head's CI run on the same branch was created (waste
+              a cancel at creation saves), and minutes of jobs that never
+              started before that moment (queue slots a cancel frees).
+  rerun       jobs of attempt >= 2 whose same-named job concluded success in
+              the previous attempt (a whole-run re-run), minutes; excluding
+              `gate` and `sweep-self`, which sweep/refresh re-run on purpose.
+  record      CI runs on record/* (and other non-fix) branches, minutes.
+  prelude     prelude job minutes by run kind (title), the wait_sources share.
+
+NULL CONTROLS (each arm's predicate applied where it must read ~0):
+  supersede-null  the same arm with "newer head" replaced by "same head_sha"
+                  restricted to code runs: twins are never superseded, so the
+                  arm must not count a run against its own head.
+  rerun-null      attempt-1 jobs read as re-runs: must be 0 by construction of
+                  the previous-attempt lookup.
+  queue-null      the queue arm on a quiet day (pass that day): waits near 0.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import collections
+import datetime as dt
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = "tvofi/heatpump_optimizer"
+
+
+def ts(s):
+    return dt.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00")) if s else None
+
+
+def gh(path):
+    for attempt in range(4):                       # a 502 from the API is retried, never counted
+        out = subprocess.run(["gh", "api", "--paginate", path], capture_output=True, text=True)
+        if out.returncode == 0:
+            break
+        time.sleep(5 * (attempt + 1))
+    else:
+        raise SystemExit(f"gh api {path}: {out.stderr.strip()}")
+    # --paginate concatenates JSON objects; split them
+    dec, i, docs, s = json.JSONDecoder(), 0, [], out.stdout
+    while i < len(s):
+        while i < len(s) and s[i].isspace():
+            i += 1
+        if i >= len(s):
+            break
+        d, i = dec.raw_decode(s, i)
+        docs.append(d)
+    return docs
+
+
+def cache_dir(a):
+    d = Path(a.cache or os.path.join(os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp"), "ci3885_queue"))
+    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    return d
+
+
+def fetch(a):
+    d = cache_dir(a)
+    runs = []
+    for doc in gh(f"repos/{REPO}/actions/runs?created={a.day}&per_page=100"):
+        runs += doc["workflow_runs"]
+    keep = [{k: r.get(k) for k in ("id", "name", "event", "head_branch", "head_sha", "status",
+                                   "conclusion", "created_at", "run_started_at", "updated_at",
+                                   "run_attempt", "display_title")} | {"actor": r["actor"]["login"]}
+            for r in runs]
+    jobs = {}
+    for r in keep:
+        js = []
+        for doc in gh(f"repos/{REPO}/actions/runs/{r['id']}/jobs?filter=all&per_page=100"):
+            js += [{k: j.get(k) for k in ("id", "name", "run_attempt", "status", "conclusion",
+                                          "created_at", "started_at", "completed_at")}
+                   for j in doc["jobs"]]
+        jobs[str(r["id"])] = js
+    (d / f"{a.day}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"runs": keep, "jobs": jobs}))
+    print(f"cached {len(keep)} runs, {sum(map(len, jobs.values()))} jobs -> {d / (a.day + '.json')}")
+
+
+def ran(j):
+    return j["conclusion"] not in (None, "skipped") and j["started_at"] and j["completed_at"] \
+        and ts(j["completed_at"]) > ts(j["started_at"])
+
+
+def mins(j):
+    return (ts(j["completed_at"]) - ts(j["started_at"])).total_seconds() / 60
+
+
+def pct(xs, p):
+    xs = sorted(xs)
+    return xs[min(len(xs) - 1, int(p * len(xs)))] if xs else 0
+
+
+def kind(r):
+    t = (r.get("display_title") or "").split()
+    return t[1] if r["name"] .startswith("CI") and len(t) > 1 else r["name"]
+
+
+def wf(r):
+    return "CI" if r["name"].startswith("CI ") else r["name"]
+
+
+def report(a):
+    data = json.loads((cache_dir(a) / f"{a.day}.json").read_text())
+    runs, jobs = data["runs"], {int(k): v for k, v in data["jobs"].items()}
+    # A re-run of one job lists EVERY job again under the new attempt, the untouched ones as
+    # copies carrying the earlier attempt's timestamps: counted, they read 1,303 copied jobs
+    # (2026-11-25) as executed re-runs. A job executed once is kept at its first attempt only.
+    out = {}
+    copies = 0
+    for rid, js in jobs.items():
+        seen, keep = set(), []
+        for j in sorted(js, key=lambda j: j["run_attempt"]):
+            key = (j["name"], j["started_at"], j["completed_at"])
+            if j["run_attempt"] > 1 and key in seen and not a.keep_copies:
+                copies += 1
+                continue
+            seen.add(key)
+            keep.append(j)
+        jobs[rid] = keep
+    out["copied_jobs_dropped"] = copies
+
+    # census
+    c = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0.0, 0])
+    edges = []
+    for r in runs:
+        js = [j for j in jobs[r["id"]] if ran(j)]
+        e = c[wf(r)]
+        e[0] += 1
+        e[1] += bool(js)
+        e[2] += sum(map(mins, js))
+        e[3] += len(js)
+        for j in js:
+            edges += [(ts(j["started_at"]), 1), (ts(j["completed_at"]), -1)]
+    peak = cur = 0
+    for _, s in sorted(edges, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1])):
+        cur += s
+        peak = max(peak, cur)
+    out["census"] = {k: {"runs": v[0], "held_runner": v[1], "runner_min": round(v[2]), "jobs": v[3]}
+                     for k, v in sorted(c.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1][2])}
+    out["peak_concurrent_jobs"] = peak
+
+    # queue
+    waits, byhour = [], collections.defaultdict(list)
+    for r in runs:
+        for j in jobs[r["id"]]:
+            if ran(j):
+                w = (ts(j["started_at"]) - ts(j["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60
+                waits.append(w)
+                byhour[j["created_at"][11:13]].append(w)
+    out["queue"] = {"jobs": len(waits), "p50_min": round(pct(waits, .5), 1), "p90_min": round(pct(waits, .9), 1),
+                    "max_min": round(max(waits or [0]), 1),
+                    "by_hour_p90": {h: round(pct(v, .9)) for h, v in sorted(byhour.items())}}
+
+    # e2e
+    e2e, first = [], []
+    for r in runs:
+        if wf(r) != "CI":
+            continue
+        js = jobs[r["id"]]
+        st = [ts(j["started_at"]) for j in js if j["run_attempt"] == 1 and ran(j)]
+        if st:
+            first.append((min(st) - ts(r["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60)
+        g = [j for j in js if j["name"] == "gate" and j["run_attempt"] == 1 and j["completed_at"]
+             and j["conclusion"] not in ("skipped", "cancelled")]
+        if g:
+            e2e.append(((ts(g[0]["completed_at"]) - ts(r["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60, kind(r)))
+    # decompose: where a run's wall clock goes. pending = run created -> first job CREATED
+    # (a concurrency group holding the run; no runner involved); queue = the run's longest
+    # job created -> started (the account's runner cap); longest = its longest job's run time.
+    dec = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))
+    for r in runs:
+        if wf(r) != "CI":
+            continue
+        js = [j for j in jobs[r["id"]] if j["run_attempt"] == 1]
+        g = [j for j in js if j["name"] == "gate" and j["completed_at"] and j["conclusion"] not in ("skipped", "cancelled")]
+        if not js or not g:
+            continue
+        k = f"{r['event']}:{kind(r)}"
+        dec[k]["pending"].append((min(ts(j["created_at"]) for j in js) - ts(r["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60)
+        q = [(ts(j["started_at"]) - ts(j["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60 for j in js if ran(j)]
+        dec[k]["queue_max"].append(max(q or [0]))
+        dec[k]["longest_job"].append(max([mins(j) for j in js if ran(j) and j["name"] != "prelude"] or [0]))
+        dec[k]["prelude"].append(max([mins(j) for j in js if j["name"] == "prelude" and ran(j)] or [0]))
+        dec[k]["e2e"].append((ts(g[0]["completed_at"]) - ts(r["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60)
+    out["decompose_p50_p90"] = {k: {m: [round(pct(v, .5)), round(pct(v, .9)), len(v)] for m, v in d.items()}
+                                for k, d in sorted(dec.items())}
+    for k in sorted({x[1] for x in e2e}):
+        v = [x[0] for x in e2e if x[1] == k]
+        out.setdefault("e2e_by_kind", {})[k] = {"n": len(v), "p50_min": round(pct(v, .5)), "p90_min": round(pct(v, .9))}
+    out["ci_first_job_wait"] = {"n": len(first), "p50_min": round(pct(first, .5)), "p90_min": round(pct(first, .9)),
+                                "max_min": round(max(first or [0]))}
+
+    # sweep
+    sw = [r for r in runs if r["name"] == "Gate sweep"]
+    held = [j for r in sw for j in jobs[r["id"]] if ran(j)]
+    ci_runs = [r for r in runs if wf(r) == "CI"]
+    attempt2 = 0
+    for r in sw:
+        cands = [x for x in ci_runs if x["head_sha"] == r["head_sha"] and ts(x["updated_at"]) <= ts(r["created_at"])]
+        if cands and max(cands, key=lambda x: x["updated_at"])["run_attempt"] > 1:
+            attempt2 += 1
+    out["sweep"] = {"runs": len(sw), "held_runner": len(held), "runner_min": round(sum(map(mins, held))),
+                    "p50_job_min": round(pct([mins(j) for j in held], .5), 1),
+                    "p90_job_min": round(pct([mins(j) for j in held], .9), 1),
+                    "after_ci_attempt_ge2": attempt2,
+                    "queue_p90_min": round(pct([(ts(j["started_at"]) - ts(j["created_at"])).total_seconds() / 60
+                                                for j in held], .9))}
+
+    # supersede (and its null)
+    def supersede(same):
+        waste = slot = 0.0
+        n = 0
+        pr = [r for r in ci_runs if r["event"] in ("pull_request", "workflow_dispatch") and r["head_branch"] != "main"]
+        for r in pr:
+            newer = [x for x in pr if x["head_branch"] == r["head_branch"] and x["id"] > r["id"]
+                     and ((x["head_sha"] == r["head_sha"] and kind(x) == "code" and kind(r) == "code") if same
+                          else x["head_sha"] != r["head_sha"])]
+            if not newer:
+                continue
+            t = min(ts(x["created_at"]) for x in newer)
+            hit = False
+            for j in jobs[r["id"]]:
+                if not ran(j):
+                    continue
+                s, e = ts(j["started_at"]), ts(j["completed_at"])
+                if e > t:
+                    waste += (e - max(s, t)).total_seconds() / 60
+                    hit = True
+                    if s > t:
+                        slot += 1
+            n += hit
+        return {"runs": n, "runner_min_after_newer_head": round(waste), "jobs_started_after_newer_head": int(slot)}
+    out["supersede"] = supersede(False)
+    out["supersede_null_same_head_code"] = supersede(True)
+
+    # rerun (and its null)
+    def rerun(null):
+        m, n, gate_m = 0.0, 0, 0.0
+        for r in runs:
+            js = jobs[r["id"]]
+            prev = {(j["name"], j["run_attempt"]): j for j in js}
+            for j in js:
+                if not ran(j) or (j["run_attempt"] != 1 if null else j["run_attempt"] < 2):
+                    continue
+                p = prev.get((j["name"], j["run_attempt"] - 1))
+                if p and p["conclusion"] == "success":
+                    if j["name"] in ("gate", "sweep-self"):
+                        gate_m += mins(j)
+                    else:
+                        m += mins(j)
+                        n += 1
+        return {"jobs": n, "runner_min": round(m), "gate_rejudge_min": round(gate_m)}
+    out["rerun_of_success"] = rerun(False)
+    out["rerun_null_attempt1"] = rerun(True)
+    att = collections.Counter(r["run_attempt"] for r in ci_runs)
+    out["ci_attempts"] = dict(sorted(att.items()))
+
+    # record
+    rec = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0.0])
+    for r in ci_runs:
+        b = (r["head_branch"] or "").split("/")[0]
+        rec[b][0] += 1
+        rec[b][1] += sum(mins(j) for j in jobs[r["id"]] if ran(j))
+    out["ci_by_branch_prefix"] = {k: {"runs": v[0], "runner_min": round(v[1])} for k, v in rec.items()}
+
+    # prelude
+    pre = collections.defaultdict(list)
+    for r in ci_runs:
+        for j in jobs[r["id"]]:
+            if j["name"] == "prelude" and ran(j):
+                pre[kind(r)].append(mins(j))
+    out["prelude"] = {k: {"n": len(v), "runner_min": round(sum(v)), "p50_min": round(pct(v, .5), 1),
+                          "p90_min": round(pct(v, .9), 1), "max_min": round(max(v), 1)} for k, v in pre.items()}
+    # job-name totals for CI
+    jn = collections.Counter()
+    for r in ci_runs:
+        for j in jobs[r["id"]]:
+            if ran(j):
+                jn[j["name"].split(" / ")[0]] += mins(j)
+    out["ci_minutes_by_unit"] = {k: round(v) for k, v in jn.most_common(15)}
+
+    # waits: runner-minutes a job held beyond its own no-wait floor (the day's p10 of that
+    # job's duration): the in-job polls and sleeps. The NULL rows are jobs with no wait in
+    # them (a compile/lint step): their excess is run-time spread, the arm's noise floor.
+    WAITERS = {"prelude": "prelude wait_sources (edit) / review", "gate": "gate judge lag wait",
+               "sweep": "Gate sweep poll/settle", "sweep-self": "sweep-self poll/settle",
+               "pr-contract / pr-contract": "pr-contract codescan_wait", "refresh": "refresh (no wait)",
+               "hassfest / hassfest": "NULL hassfest", "tests / typing": "NULL typing",
+               "validate / validate-hacs": "NULL validate"}
+    w = collections.defaultdict(list)
+    for r in runs:
+        for j in jobs[r["id"]]:
+            if ran(j) and j["name"] in WAITERS:
+                w[j["name"]].append((mins(j), kind(r)))
+    out["waits"] = {}
+    for name, v in w.items():
+        floor = pct([m for m, _ in v], .1)
+        excess = [max(0.0, m - floor) for m, _ in v]
+        out["waits"][WAITERS[name]] = {"n": len(v), "runner_min": round(sum(m for m, _ in v)), "floor_min": round(floor, 2),
+                                       "excess_min": round(sum(excess)), "jobs_over_5min_excess": sum(e > 5 for e in excess)}
+    print(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=("fetch", "report"))
+    ap.add_argument("day")
+    ap.add_argument("--cache")
+    ap.add_argument("--keep-copies", action="store_true",
+                    help="the perturbation: count re-run listings' copied jobs as executed")
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    (fetch if a.cmd == "fetch" else report)(a)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/hotfile_conflicts.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/hotfile_conflicts.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..caaa5d774d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/hotfile_conflicts.py
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Replay PR-side main merges and count conflicts per file, before and after (R11-OWNER-HOTFILE-COUNTS).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/hotfile_conflicts.py [--main <sha>] [--days 10]
+
+The window: every pull request merged into ``--main``'s first-parent history in
+the ``--days`` before ``--main``'s commit time. For each, every merge commit on
+the pull request's side whose subject merges main (``origin/main``, ``branch
+'main'``) is re-merged with ``git merge-tree --write-tree`` three ways:
+
+  * ``before`` -- under the merge's own first parent's ``.gitattributes``
+    (``--attr-source``), the routing the merge actually had;
+  * ``driver`` -- under this checkout's ``.gitattributes``, so the D6 register
+    goes to ``tools/merge/ledger_merge.py``'s row arm;
+  * ``after`` -- the ``driver`` merge, and each hot text file re-merged with
+    ``git merge-file`` after the passages main has stopped storing are replaced,
+    on all three sides, by main's current text of that passage (ANCHORS): what
+    the merge would have met had the file carried main's form.
+
+A file absent from ANCHORS is never rewritten, so its ``after`` count is its
+``driver`` count; ``other files`` is the null control that the routing moves
+nothing it does not route. The merge driver must be installed
+(``python3 tools/merge/ledger_merge.py --install``) and git must be 2.40 or
+later; anything but merge-tree's exit 0 or 1 refuses (exit 2).
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import collections
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(__file__)
+HOT = (
+    "tests/deployment_shape.py",
+    "docs/architecture.md",
+    "dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.json",
+    "dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.md",
+    "dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py",
+)
+#: Per hot text file, the passages (start anchor, end anchor) main no longer
+#: stores a derived value in: everything from the start line up to, not
+#: including, the end line is replaced by main's current text of it.
+ANCHORS = {
+    "tests/deployment_shape.py": [("COST OF THE SHAPE", "    python tests/deployment_shape.py")],
+    "dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py": [
+        ("    RESULT arch_", "INSTRUMENTED SYMBOLS"),
+        ("_disk = sorted(", 'claim("C35"'),
+    ],
+    "docs/architecture.md": [
+        ("knows nothing about Home Assistant:", "function, and the rest take numbers"),
+        ("## The Home Assistant boundary", "`config_flow`, `coordinator`"),
+        ("clock function was injected.", "directly by `tests/features.py`"),
+    ],
+}
+MAIN_MERGE = re.compile(r"origin/main|branch 'main'")
+
+
+def git(*a: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
+    r = subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if check and r.returncode != 0:
+        sys.exit(f"REFUSED: git {' '.join(a[:3])} exited {r.returncode}: {r.stderr.strip()[:200]}")
+    return r
+
+
+def passage(text: str, start: str, end: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    lines = text.split("\n")
+    s = next((i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith(start)), None)
+    if s is None:
+        return None
+    e = next((i for i in range(s + 1, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith(end)), None)
+    return None if e is None else (s, e)
+
+
+def normalise(text: str, path: str, main_text: str) -> str:
+    for start, end in ANCHORS.get(path, ()):
+        here, there = passage(text, start, end), passage(main_text, start, end)
+        if here is None or there is None:
+            continue
+        lines, mlines = text.split("\n"), main_text.split("\n")
+        text = "\n".join(lines[:here[0]] + mlines[there[0]:there[1]] + lines[here[1]:])
+    return text
+
+
+def conflicted(attr: str, p1: str, p2: str) -> list[str]:
+    r = git(f"--attr-source={attr}", "merge-tree", "--write-tree", "--name-only",
+            "--no-messages", p1, p2, check=False)
+    if r.returncode not in (0, 1):
+        sys.exit(f"REFUSED: merge-tree exited {r.returncode} on {p1[:12]} {p2[:12]}: "
+                 f"{r.stderr.strip()[:200]} (git 2.40+ for --attr-source)")
+    return r.stdout.splitlines()[1:] if r.returncode == 1 else []
+
+
+def blob(rev: str, path: str) -> str:
+    r = git("show", f"{rev}:{path}", check=False)
+    return r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else ""
+
+
+def text_conflicts(path: str, base: str, p1: str, p2: str, main: str) -> bool:
+    m = blob(main, path)
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        files = []
+        for name, rev in (("ours", p1), ("base", base), ("theirs", p2)):
+            f = Path(td, name)
+            f.write_text(normalise(blob(rev, path), path, m))
+            files.append(str(f))
+        r = subprocess.run(["git", "merge-file", "-q", "-p", *files], capture_output=True)
+    if r.returncode < 0 or r.returncode > 127:
+        sys.exit(f"REFUSED: merge-file exited {r.returncode} on {path}")
+    return r.returncode != 0
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--main", default="ef797d794017c98f7fb2d8a168d7de63d435ef3b")
+    ap.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=10)
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    main_sha = git("rev-parse", a.main).stdout.strip()
+    end = int(git("log", "-1", "--format=%ct", main_sha).stdout)
+    since = end - a.days * 86400
+    prs = [ln.split()[0] for ln in git("log", "--merges", "--first-parent", "--format=%H %ct",
+                                       main_sha).stdout.splitlines()
+           if int(ln.split()[1]) >= since]
+    merges = []
+    for pr in prs:
+        side = git("rev-list", "--merges", "--format=%H %P%n%s", f"{pr}^1..{pr}^2").stdout
+        lines = [ln for ln in side.splitlines() if not ln.startswith("commit ")]
+        for head, subj in zip(lines[::2], lines[1::2]):
+            if MAIN_MERGE.search(subj):
+                merges.append(head.split()[:3])
+    count = {k: collections.Counter() for k in ("before", "driver", "after")}
+    with_any = collections.Counter()
+    for m, p1, p2 in merges:
+        before = set(conflicted(p1, p1, p2))
+        driver = set(conflicted("HEAD", p1, p2))
+        base = git("merge-base", p1, p2).stdout.split()[0]
+        after = {f for f in driver
+                 if f not in ANCHORS or text_conflicts(f, base, p1, p2, main_sha)}
+        for k, s in (("before", before), ("driver", driver), ("after", after)):
+            count[k].update(s)
+            with_any[k] += bool(s)
+    print(f"window: {len(prs)} pull requests merged into {main_sha[:10]}'s first parent "
+          f"in {a.days} days; {len(merges)} main merges on their branches")
+    print(f"{'file':44} {'before':>6} {'driver':>6} {'after':>6}")
+    for f in HOT:
+        print(f"{f:44} {count['before'][f]:>6} {count['driver'][f]:>6} {count['after'][f]:>6}")
+    other = {k: sum(n for f, n in c.items() if f not in HOT) for k, c in count.items()}
+    print(f"{'other files':44} {other['before']:>6} {other['driver']:>6} {other['after']:>6}")
+    print(f"{'merges with any conflict':44} {with_any['before']:>6} {with_any['driver']:>6} "
+          f"{with_any['after']:>6}")
+    for f in sorted({f for c in count.values() for f in c if f not in HOT}):
+        if len({count[k][f] for k in count}) > 1:
+            print(f"OTHER-FILE-MOVED {f}: " + " ".join(f"{k}={count[k][f]}" for k in count))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py
index e5d2147735..a6740a8afb 100644
--- a/dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py
@@ -100,6 +100,8 @@ def expr_value(e: str, tmp: str) -> str:
         "needs.closure-scope.outputs.case == 'scoped' && 'scoped' || 'full'": "full",
         "inputs.gate_scope == 'auto' && 'auto' || 'full'": "full",
         "inputs.base || 'main'": "main",
+        # A pull_request run's prelude leaves range_base empty (a push's light range sets it).
+        "inputs.range_base || format('origin/{0}', inputs.base || 'main')": "origin/main",
     }
     if e.startswith("github.event.pull_request.base.sha"):
         return "origin/main"
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/prepr_6d_arms.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/prepr_6d_arms.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..27563ff39a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/prepr_6d_arms.py
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Step 6d's predictor timed per arm over one fixed diff, at one tree (R10-RCA-OPEN-PREPR-SLOW, C4).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/prepr_6d_arms.py <commit> [<file> ...]
+
+In a throwaway worktree of <commit>, commits one comment line appended to each
+<file> (default `TOUCH`, the paths of slim-p2's diff at 6671786843 that a gate
+cannot scope, code and prose, that still exist), then runs that tree's own
+`tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base <commit> --record-self-tests`, prepr's 6d call,
+with each arm, each restoring job of GRADER and each STEP REPLAY replay timed.
+The diff is the same bytes at any <commit> where the files exist, so two
+commits run on one host, seconds apart, compare the predictor and nothing else:
+`<merge base>` is the before, `<fixed head>` the after. Prints one
+`ARM <name> <s>` line per arm, `JOB` per restoring job, `REPLAY` per replay,
+then `wall_s`, `predict_sha1` (a sha1 of the sorted PREDICT lines: the
+before/after identity check `open_prepr_6d.sh` prints) and `predict_lines`,
+`left_to_ci` (the steps the replay budget left to CI) and the predictor's
+last line. Hours at a full diff on a 4-CPU container; run it in the background.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+TOUCH = (".github/workflows/governance.yml", ".github/workflows/tests.yml", "tests/entities.py",
+         "tools/pr/ci_predict.py", "tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py", "tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh",
+         "tools/audit/seat/bus.sh", "tools/audit/seat/postmerge.py", "tools/pr/app_approve.sh",
+         "dev/governance/roles/fixer.md", "CLAUDE.md")
+
+# Runs inside the throwaway tree: wraps the module's own functions, changes none.
+TIMER = r'''
+import sys, time
+sys.path.insert(0, "tools/pr")
+import ci_predict as cp
+def say(*a):
+    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+def wrap(name, label):
+    f = getattr(cp, name, None)
+    if f is None:
+        return
+    def timed(*a, **k):
+        t = time.monotonic(); r = f(*a, **k)
+        say(label(a, r), f"{time.monotonic() - t:.1f}")
+        return r
+    setattr(cp, name, timed)
+wrap("ci_tree_run", lambda a, r: f"JOB {a[2]}")
+wrap("replay_step", lambda a, r: f"REPLAY rc={r}")
+arms = cp.run_arms
+def run_arms(arms_, only, record):
+    out = []
+    for name, arm in arms_:
+        if cp.arm_runs(name, only, record):
+            t = time.monotonic(); p = arm(); out += p
+            say(f"ARM {name}", f"{time.monotonic() - t:.1f}")
+    return out
+cp.run_arms = run_arms
+sys.exit(cp.main(sys.argv[1:]))
+'''
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    if not argv:
+        print(__doc__)
+        return 2
+    commit, files = argv[0], tuple(argv[1:]) or TOUCH
+    repo = Path(subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], text=True).strip())
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        wt = Path(d) / "t"
+        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", str(wt), commit], check=True)
+        try:
+            sha = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, text=True).strip()
+            held = [f for f in files if (wt / f).is_file()]
+            for f in held:
+                with open(wt / f, "a") as fh:
+                    fh.write("\n<!-- prepr_6d_arms touch -->\n" if f.endswith(".md") else "\n# prepr_6d_arms touch\n")
+            subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=h", "-c", "user.email=h@h", "commit", "-qam",
+                            "prepr_6d_arms touch"], cwd=wt, check=True)
+            (Path(d) / "timer.py").write_text(TIMER)
+            env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH="tests/hastub")
+            t = time.monotonic()
+            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(Path(d) / "timer.py"), "--base", sha, "--record-self-tests"],
+                               cwd=wt, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
+            wall = time.monotonic() - t
+        finally:
+            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt)])
+    timed = [l for l in r.stderr.splitlines() if l.startswith(("ARM ", "JOB ", "REPLAY "))]
+    pred = sorted(l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("PREDICT"))
+    left = [l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("NOTE    LEFT TO CI")]
+    print(f"at={sha} touched={len(held)} rc={r.returncode}")
+    print("\n".join(timed))
+    print(f"wall_s={wall:.0f}")
+    print(f"predict_sha1={hashlib.sha1(''.join(l + chr(10) for l in pred).encode()).hexdigest()} "
+          f"predict_lines={len(pred)}")
+    print(f"left_to_ci={left[0].split()[4] if left else 0}")
+    print((r.stdout.strip().splitlines() or ["(no output)"])[-1])
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_dead_state_mutants.sh b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_dead_state_mutants.sh
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..b307f3bdbe
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_dead_state_mutants.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,244 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# r11_dead_state_mutants.sh -- MUTANT_CMD for the R11-SEAM-dead-state diff's mutants.
+#
+# The diff deleted state that production stores and nothing reads; its mutants (a deleted call, a
+# swapped index, a dropped statement on the touched lines) are each held by one tests/features.py
+# block. This chains those blocks through tools/audit/seat/features_block.py, which runs one block of
+# the script instead of the tens of minutes the whole of it takes. A block reads names that earlier
+# parts of features.py define, so each call carries the --prelude lines that bind them (the
+# --emit-prelude derivation costs 7-22 s a block, too slow to repeat per mutant; block 8's derived
+# prelude is embedded below). The command exits 0 only when every block passes, so a mutant is
+# KILLED when any block fails.
+#
+#     bash dev/audit/harnesses/r11_dead_state_mutants.sh
+#
+# As the mutant driver's command (run from the repository root):
+#     python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD" \
+#         --cmd "bash dev/audit/harnesses/r11_dead_state_mutants.sh" --max-mutants 40 --report-only
+#
+# Exits 0 on an unmutated tree and 1 at the first block that fails (its FAIL lines follow).
+set -euo pipefail
+export PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub
+T=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+FB="python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py"
+n=0
+blk() { # <START> <END> <--prelude args...>: one features.py block
+  local s=$1 e=$2; shift 2; n=$((n + 1))
+  $FB "$@" "$s" "$e" >"$T/r$n.log" 2>&1 \
+    || { echo "block $n ($s) FAILED"; grep -a 'FAIL\|Error' "$T/r$n.log" | head -5 | cut -c1-240; exit 1; }
+}
+# The T4 helpers (_t4_coord and friends) that features.py defines ahead of the sysid blocks.
+T4="exec('_T4_DATA = {' + open('tests/features.py').read().split('_T4_DATA = {',1)[1].split('# -- \`_entity_state\`',1)[0])"
+SIDP=(--prelude 'import ast as _p5_ast' --prelude 'import sys as _p5_sys' --prelude 'import logging as _p5_logging, inspect as _p5_inspect'
+  --prelude 'import heatpump_optimizer.coordinator as _p5_coord_mod' --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.coordinator import HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator'
+  --prelude 'from harness import FakeEntry' --prelude 'import asyncio as _asyncio' --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer import sysid as _SysIdModule'
+  --prelude 'from dataclasses import replace as _dc_replace' --prelude "$T4")
+HARN=(--prelude 'from harness import FakeEntry as _FakeEntry, FakeHass as _FakeHass' --prelude 'import asyncio as _asyncio')
+COORD=(--prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.coordinator import HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator as _Coord')
+
+# curve_learning.record_miss, from record_day
+blk '# --- #2 the heat-curve bias' '# --- round-5 D3-08' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.curve_learning import BIAS_MIN, COMFORT_MARGIN_C, DAYS_PER_STEP, STEP_K, CurveLearner'
+# coordinator record_miss, from _track_curve_comfort
+blk '_T2_LEARNER_T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 15, 6, 0, 0)' '# The quiet-period learner reads the SOLVED plan' \
+  "${HARN[@]}" "${COORD[@]}" --prelude 'from types import SimpleNamespace as _NS' --prelude 'from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util'
+# async_shutdown awaits the background tasks it tracks
+blk '# D1-02 hygiene: fire-and-forget tasks are tracked' '# A save that changes nothing must not reload.' \
+  "${HARN[@]}" --prelude '_LC_DATA = {"price_source": "entity", "price_entity": "sensor.prices", "weather_entity": "weather.home"}'
+# optimizer._peak_window_factors
+blk 'R.section("R8-D2-s2-01 — the capacity bill' '# --- #1512 x #1499: the no-meter arm' \
+  "${HARN[@]}" "${COORD[@]}" --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer import grid_fee as _gf'
+# sysid.adoption_decision and its coordinator caller
+blk '# #1525: the adoption gate lives in one pure function' 'R.section("Actuation routing: every accepted domain' "${SIDP[@]}"
+# SystemIdentification.arm's slab gate
+blk '_g1401_plant = ThermalParameters()' 'R.section("#1329: the sysid arm/adopt gate opens' "${SIDP[@]}" \
+  --prelude 'NOW = datetime(2026, 2, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)' --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.sysid import SystemIdentification' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import ThermalParameters'
+# identify_slab's series unpack
+blk '# -- the sysid-estimator wave, first act' '# -- the three service entry points, and what each one costs' "${SIDP[@]}" \
+  --prelude 'NOW = datetime(2026, 2, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)' --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.sysid import SystemIdentification' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import ThermalParameters' --prelude 'from profiles import house as _grad_house' \
+  --prelude "exec('from stress import BUILDINGS as _b942' + open('tests/features.py').read().split('from stress import BUILDINGS as _b942',1)[1].split('_g942_unseeded = ',1)[0])" \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer import presets' --prelude '_bar = _SysIdModule.UA_ADOPTION_HALFWIDTH_BAR'
+# identify's two-column lstsq fallback
+blk 'R.section("W5-G8 i: the system-identification experiment' '# -- W5-G8 j: the wood night advisory'
+# flow_meter.observe_water: the fold and the supply slot (prelude derived with --emit-prelude)
+cat >"$T/fm.py" <<'EOF_PRE'
+NOW = datetime(2026, 2, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
+from dataclasses import replace
+from harness import FakeEntry, FakeHass
+from heatpump_optimizer.coordinator import HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator
+from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+_T2_DATA = {"tibber_token": "x", "weather_entity": "weather.home"}
+def _t2_coord(**config):
+    """A live coordinator over the fake bus, with config overrides applied."""
+    return HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator(
+        FakeHass(), FakeEntry(data=dict(_T2_DATA, **config))
+    )
+def _t2_count_saves(coord):
+    """Record every thermal-learning save, so "it persisted" is observable."""
+    coord._t2_saves = []
+    inner = coord._async_save_thermal_learning
+
+    async def counted():
+        coord._t2_saves.append(coord._buffer_cooling_rate)
+        return await inner()
+
+    coord._async_save_thermal_learning = counted
+_T2_HOUSE_CFG = {
+    "indoor_temp_entity": "sensor.indoor",
+    "outdoor_temp_entity": "sensor.outdoor",
+}
+_T2_TWO_ZONE_CFG = {
+    "upper_floor_thermal_mass": 3.0,
+    "lower_floor_thermal_mass": 8.0,
+    "lower_floor_temp_entity": "sensor.lower",
+}
+_T2_HOUSE_STATE = ThermalState(
+    room_temperature=21.0,
+    upper_floor_temperature=21.0,
+    lower_floor_temperature=20.0,
+    slab_temperature=27.0,
+    outdoor_temperature=-5.0,
+)
+def _t2_house(
+    *,
+    observed=20.9,
+    lower=None,
+    hours=0.5,
+    power=2.0,
+    outdoor=-5.0,
+    two_zone=False,
+    **config,
+):
+    """A coordinator holding one replayable interval, not yet learned from."""
+    cfg = dict(_T2_HOUSE_CFG)
+    if two_zone:
+        cfg.update(_T2_TWO_ZONE_CFG)
+    cfg.update(config)
+    c = _t2_coord(**cfg)
+    _t2_count_saves(c)
+    previous = replace(_T2_HOUSE_STATE, outdoor_temperature=outdoor)
+    c._last_house_sample = previous
+    c._last_house_sample_time = dt_util.now() - timedelta(hours=hours)
+    c._current_state = replace(
+        previous,
+        room_temperature=observed,
+        upper_floor_temperature=observed,
+        lower_floor_temperature=(
+            previous.lower_floor_temperature if lower is None else lower
+        ),
+    )
+    c._current_action = {"power": power}
+    return c
+def _t2_drive(coord, method):
+    """Run one learner and capture anything that escapes it."""
+    coord._t2_escaped = None
+    try:
+        _asyncio.run(getattr(coord, method)(coord._close_fabric_interval()))
+    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001
+        coord._t2_escaped = err
+    return coord
+from heatpump_optimizer import const as _fb_const
+from heatpump_optimizer import flow_meter as _fm
+from heatpump_optimizer.inputs import (  # noqa: E402
+    InputReader as _fmReader,
+    normalize_flow_kg_s as _fm_norm,
+)
+_FM_LEARN_KW = 5.22
+_FM_FLOW_CFG = {
+    _fb_const.CONF_FLOW_METER_ENTITY: "sensor.flow",
+    _fb_const.CONF_HEAT_PUMP_SUPPLY_TEMP_ENTITY: "sensor.sup",
+    _fb_const.CONF_HEAT_PUMP_RETURN_TEMP_ENTITY: "sensor.ret",
+}
+def _fm_plant(coord, flow="15.0", unit="L/min", age_min=1):
+    """Plant this cycle's three water states and run the production fold."""
+    coord.hass.states.set(
+        "sensor.flow",
+        # Polled: re-reported ``age_min`` ago (#2234).
+        FakeState(flow, last_updated=minutes_ago(age_min + 3, NOW),
+                  last_reported=minutes_ago(age_min, NOW), unit=unit),
+    )
+    coord.hass.states.set(
+        "sensor.sup",
+        FakeState("45.0", last_updated=minutes_ago(1, NOW), unit="°C"),
+    )
+    coord.hass.states.set(
+        "sensor.ret",
+        FakeState("40.0", last_updated=minutes_ago(1, NOW), unit="°C"),
+    )
+    # The outranked arm configures the pump's power meter, and its learner has
+    # to reach the replay for that arm's refusal to mean something other than
+    # "the learner never ran": the fixture builds no cycle, so the meter's
+    # value is planted the way `_update_current_state` would have left it.
+    coord.hass.states.set(
+        "sensor.hp_power",
+        FakeState("2000", last_updated=minutes_ago(1, NOW), unit="W"),
+    )
+    reader = _fmReader(coord.hass, coord.effective_config, now=lambda: NOW)
+    _fm.observe_water(coord._flow_bias, reader, coord.effective_config)
+    return coord
+def _fm_spy(coord):
+    """The next replay's call to ``simulate_step``: its kwargs and its result."""
+    seen = {"kwargs": {}, "state": None}
+    real = coord._thermal_model.simulate_step
+
+    def spy(*args, **kwargs):
+        seen["kwargs"] = kwargs
+        seen["state"] = real(*args, **kwargs)
+        return seen["state"]
+
+    coord._thermal_model.simulate_step = spy
+    return seen
+def _fm_replay(
+    method,
+    *,
+    flow_cfg=True,
+    two_zone=False,
+    action=None,
+    config=None,
+    meter=None,
+    **plant,
+):
+    """One frozen-clock learner run over one planted interval.
+
+    Frozen because the fit is a Newton step on ``dt_hours`` and a live clock
+    leaves whatever gap the scheduler happens to have (#812's note above).
+    Returns ``(seen, coordinator)``.
+    """
+    dt_util.freeze(NOW)
+    try:
+        cfg = dict(_FM_FLOW_CFG) if flow_cfg else {}
+        cfg.update(config or {})
+        coord = _t2_house(two_zone=two_zone, **cfg)
+        if action is not None:
+            coord._current_action = dict(action)
+        if meter is not None:
+            coord._measured_power = float(meter)
+        _fm_plant(coord, **plant)
+        seen = _fm_spy(coord)
+        _t2_drive(coord, method)
+    finally:
+        dt_util.freeze(None)
+    return seen, coord
+_HOUSE_LEARNER = "_async_learn_house_heat_loss"
+_LOWER_LEARNER = "_async_learn_lower_floor_loss"
+EOF_PRE
+blk '_fm_seen, _fm_coord = _fm_replay(_HOUSE_LEARNER)' '# The precedence rule and the refused-reading paths' \
+  "${HARN[@]}" --prelude "exec(open('$T/fm.py').read())"
+# optimizer._build_result's set-point list
+blk "# The tank's ceiling is a hard constraint in the solve" '# and they must lead the multi-start list.' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer import mixing_valve as _mv' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import HeatPumpOptimizer as _StoreOpt, OptimizationConfig as _StoreCfg' \
+  --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import WeatherSeries' \
+  --prelude 'def _WS(outdoor, wind=None, rain=None, solar=None, humidity=None, ext=None): return WeatherSeries(outdoor_temps=outdoor, wind_speeds=wind, precipitation=rain, solar_radiation=solar, humidity=humidity, external_heat_kw=ext)'
+# coordinator._record_accuracy's one frequency sample
+blk 'R.section("Free heat skips the accuracy sample (D7-05)")' '# --- D7-03 (#279): open window skips the accuracy sample' \
+  --prelude 'from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util' --prelude 'from harness import FakeEntry as _FakeEntry, FakeHass as _FakeHass' "${COORD[@]}" \
+  --prelude '_METER = {"sensor.indoor": FakeState("21.0", unit="°C"), "sensor.outdoor": FakeState("-5.0", unit="°C"), "sensor.house_power": FakeState("6500", unit="W"), "sensor.hp_power": FakeState("2000", unit="W")}' \
+  --prelude 'def _t2_coord(states=None, **extra): return _Coord(_FakeHass(dict(_METER, **(states or {}))), _FakeEntry(data={"tibber_token": "x", "weather_entity": "weather.home", "indoor_temp_entity": "sensor.indoor", "outdoor_temp_entity": "sensor.outdoor", **extra}))'
+# optimizer._optimize_with_dhw's baseline economics: every DHW-enabled solve reaches it
+python3 tests/manual_plan.py >"$T/manual_plan.log" 2>&1 \
+  || { echo "tests/manual_plan.py FAILED"; grep -a 'FAIL\|Error' "$T/manual_plan.log" | head -5 | cut -c1-240; exit 1; }
+echo "r11_dead_state_mutants: $n blocks and tests/manual_plan.py passed"
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_balance.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_balance.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c547b7faa0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_balance.py
@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+"""The fast lane's shard balance, priced in CI seconds (R11-CI-CASE-SELECT P2, #3885).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_balance.py LOGDIR [--seed N]
+
+LOGDIR holds `fast` job logs of FULL push runs (no `MODE: SCOPED` line), one file each, as
+`dev/audit/harnesses/ci_script_seconds.py`'s job_log returns them. Each script's price is its
+median over those logs' closing wall-clock tables. A shard's wall is run.sh's own shape over the
+scripts it owns: the three lanes (units, golden, e2e; each lane's scripts in sequence, the lanes
+side by side) and then the stress lane alone.
+
+Prints, each with the rule that produced it:
+  CALIBRATION  the same model over the unsharded suite against the logs' median TOTAL line;
+  PLAN         tools/ci/shards.py's full plan at HEAD: each shard's modelled wall, the makespan;
+  NULL random  the makespan of 200 random assignments to the same shard count (median, best);
+  FLOOR        the longest single script's median, which no script-level shard can beat;
+  SPLIT        per script tests/case_select.py splits: the best two-way contiguous span split,
+               each half run with its `needs` closure (what a sound split must re-run), as the
+               larger half's share of the script's recorded span seconds; NULL: the same split
+               with every `needs` edge dropped (the unsound split).
+EXPECTED RESULT: the plan's makespan is within 10% of FLOOR and under the random null's median;
+the unsharded model reads within 20% of the logs' median TOTAL (each script at its own median,
+summed along a lane, overstates a run whose scripts drew a fast host together); SPLIT reads above
+0.9 for both scripts. Its null reads near 0.5 for features.py (the needs closure, not the
+splitter, keeps it whole) and stays high for entities.py, whose one span `#558 D6 numeric schedule
+companion` holds most of its seconds.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import random
+import re
+import statistics
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(__file__)
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "ci"))
+import shards  # noqa: E402
+
+LANE_FN = re.compile(r"^lane_(\w+)\(\) \{$")
+
+
+def lanes_of_run_sh() -> dict[str, str]:
+    """script -> the run.sh lane function its run line sits in."""
+    out, lane = {}, None
+    for line in (ROOT / "tests" / "run.sh").read_text().splitlines():
+        m = LANE_FN.match(line)
+        if m:
+            lane = m.group(1)
+            continue
+        if line.startswith("}"):
+            lane = None
+        m = shards._RUN_LINE.match(line)
+        if m and lane:
+            out.setdefault(m.group(2), lane)
+    return out
+
+
+def medians(logdir: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, float], list[float], int]:
+    per: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
+    totals, used = [], 0
+    for f in sorted(logdir.iterdir()):
+        t = f.read_text(errors="replace")
+        if "MODE: SCOPED" in t or "########## wall clock ##########" not in t:
+            continue
+        used += 1
+        table = t.split("########## wall clock ##########", 1)[1]
+        one: dict[str, int] = {}          # a script's lines in one run summed (env_drift runs twice)
+        for line in table.splitlines():
+            m = re.search(r"\s(\d+)s\s+TOTAL", line)
+            if m:
+                totals.append(float(m.group(1)))
+                break
+            m = re.search(r"\s(\d+)s\s+\S+ (.*)$", line)
+            if m:
+                s = next((a for a in m.group(2).split() if a.startswith("tests/")), None)
+                if s:
+                    one[s] = one.get(s, 0) + int(m.group(1))
+        for s, v in one.items():
+            per.setdefault(s, []).append(v)
+    return {s: statistics.median(v) for s, v in per.items()}, totals, used
+
+
+def wall(owned: set[str], price: dict[str, float], lane: dict[str, str]) -> float:
+    by = {}
+    for s in owned:
+        by.setdefault(lane.get(s, "units"), 0.0)
+        by[lane.get(s, "units")] += price.get(s, 0.0)
+    return max([v for k, v in by.items() if k != "stress"], default=0.0) + by.get("stress", 0.0)
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    logdir = Path(argv[0])
+    seed = int(argv[argv.index("--seed") + 1]) if "--seed" in argv else 0
+    price, totals, used = medians(logdir)
+    lane = lanes_of_run_sh()
+    scripts, always = shards.suite_scripts((ROOT / "tests" / "run.sh").read_text())
+    print(f"logs read: {used} FULL fast logs; scripts priced: {len(price)}")
+    model = wall(set(scripts), price, lane)
+    print(f"CALIBRATION unsharded model {model:.0f}s vs median TOTAL {statistics.median(totals):.0f}s "
+          f"(ratio {model / statistics.median(totals):.3f})")
+    known = shards.timings(shards._show("HEAD", "tests/closures.json"),
+                           shards._show("HEAD", "tests/case_closures.json"))
+    p = shards.plan(scripts, always, shards.priced(scripts, known), None)
+    n = p["n"]
+    walls = [wall({s for s, k in p["s"].items() if k == i}, price, lane) for i in range(1, n + 1)]
+    print(f"PLAN {n} shards: " + ", ".join(f"{i}/{n}={w:.0f}s" for i, w in enumerate(walls, 1))
+          + f"; makespan {max(walls):.0f}s, spread max/min {max(walls) / max(min(walls), 1):.2f}")
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    nulls = []
+    for _ in range(200):
+        a = {s: rng.randint(1, n) for s in scripts}
+        nulls.append(max(wall({s for s in scripts if a[s] == i}, price, lane) for i in range(1, n + 1)))
+    print(f"NULL random ({n} shards, 200 draws, seed {seed}): median makespan {statistics.median(nulls):.0f}s, "
+          f"best {min(nulls):.0f}s")
+    top = max(price, key=price.get)
+    print(f"FLOOR longest script {top} {price[top]:.0f}s")
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tests"))
+    import case_select  # noqa: PLC0415
+    table = case_select.load()
+    for script in case_select.SCRIPTS:
+        e = case_select.entry(table, script)
+        sec = {k: v["seconds"] for k, v in e["spans"].items()}
+        ids, tot = list(sec), sum(sec.values())
+        for label, need in (("sound", {k: set(v["needs"]) for k, v in e["spans"].items()}),
+                            ("NULL no-needs", {k: set() for k in ids})):
+            def clos(start):
+                out, st = set(start), list(start)
+                while st:
+                    for x in need[st.pop()]:
+                        if x not in out:
+                            out.add(x)
+                            st.append(x)
+                return sum(sec[i] for i in out)
+            best = min(max(clos(ids[:k]), clos(ids[k:])) for k in range(1, len(ids)))
+            print(f"SPLIT {script} {label}: larger half {best:.0f}s of {tot:.0f}s recorded = {best / tot:.3f}")
+    print("PRICES " + json.dumps({s: price[s] for s in sorted(price, key=price.get, reverse=True)[:8]}))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_mutants.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_mutants.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..5c51cac99a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_mutants.py
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+"""The fast shards' mutation proof (R11-CI-CASE-SELECT P2, #3885).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_mutants.py WORKTREE
+
+WORKTREE is a checkout of the head under test, never one a suite is running in: each mutant
+deletes or inverts one production predicate in place, runs the self-test that closes over it,
+prints KILLED with the failing check names (or SURVIVED), and restores the file. The BASELINE
+lines are the same self-tests on the unmutated tree, the null control.
+EXPECTED RESULT: every mutant KILLED; every BASELINE rc=0.
+"""
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+W = Path(sys.argv[1])
+MUTANTS = [
+    ("gate: the fast name is not expanded into shards", "tools/ci/gate.py",
+     '.extend(fast if (u, n) == ("tests", FAST) else [n])', '.append(n)',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/gate.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("gate: a malformed shard list is not refused", "tools/ci/gate.py",
+     '    if why_fast:\n        return False, [why_fast]\n', '',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/gate.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("shards.check: an empty shard is accepted", "tools/ci/shards.py",
+     '    return set(s.values()) == set(range(1, n + 1))', '    return True',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("shards.route: a shard of another count is accepted", "tools/ci/shards.py",
+     'if p["n"] != n or not 1 <= k <= n:', 'if not 1 <= k <= n:',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("shards.timings: a failed run's seconds are kept", "tools/ci/shards.py",
+     'rec.get("rc", 0) != 0 or ', '',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("shards.priced: an untimed script is dropped", "tools/ci/shards.py",
+     'return {s: known.get(s, default) for s in scripts}', 'return {s: known[s] for s in scripts if s in known}',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("closure.PRODUCERS: the setup render loses its writer", "tests/closure.py",
+     '    "tests/setup_qa_render.mjs": ["tests/plan_view.py"],\n', '',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"]),
+    ("prelude: the planner's outputs are not emitted", "tools/ci/prelude.py",
+     '        out.update(fast(', '        (fast(',
+     ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/prelude.py", "--self-test"]),
+]
+for name, rel, old, new, cmd in MUTANTS:
+    p = W / rel
+    orig = p.read_text()
+    assert orig.count(old) == 1, (name, orig.count(old))
+    p.write_text(orig.replace(old, new))
+    try:
+        r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=W, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+        out = r.stdout + r.stderr
+        fails = [ln.strip() for ln in out.splitlines() if ln.strip().startswith(("FAIL", "Traceback"))]
+        verdict = "KILLED" if r.returncode != 0 and fails else "SURVIVED"
+        print(f"{verdict} [{name}] rc={r.returncode}")
+        for f in fails[:4]:
+            print(f"    {f[:170]}")
+    finally:
+        p.write_text(orig)
+# baseline: every closure green with no mutant applied
+for cmd in (["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/gate.py", "--self-test"], ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"],
+            ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/prelude.py", "--self-test"]):
+    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=W, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+    print(f"BASELINE rc={r.returncode} {(r.stdout.strip().splitlines() or [''])[-1]}")
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_random.sh b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_random.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..06de5d58c7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_random.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# The fast shards' independence proof (R11-CI-CASE-SELECT P2, #3885), run once.
+#
+#   bash dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_random.sh SEED OUTDIR [N]
+#
+# Draws a RANDOM assignment of every script run.sh names to N shards (default 3; the
+# PRODUCERS groups -- the plan payload's writer and its readers -- drawn as one unit, the one
+# dependency the planner keeps), then runs tests/run.sh once per shard, one after another, each
+# exactly as CI's fast job runs it (GOLDEN_MODE=drift, RUN_PART=fast, GATE_SCOPE=full, the
+# shard's HPO_FAST_SHARD and HPO_FAST_PLAN). Each shard's log lands in OUTDIR.
+# EXPECTED RESULT: every shard exits 0 and the union of the scripts the shards ran is every
+# script one unsharded run runs (the RAN line), with no script run twice (the TWICE line empty):
+# no script depends on another having run in the same job, beyond the group drawn together.
+# Null: a draw that splits plan_view.py from card.mjs (SPLIT_PRODUCERS=1) fails card.mjs.
+set -u
+SEED="$1"; OUT="$2"; N="${3:-3}"
+repo_root() {
+  local d="$1"
+  if [ -f "$d" ]; then
+    d=$(dirname "$d")
+  fi
+  d=$(cd "$d" && pwd) || return 1
+  while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do
+    if [ -f "$d/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json" ]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$d"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    d=$(dirname "$d")
+  done
+  printf 'no repository root above %s\n' "$1" >&2
+  return 1
+}
+ROOT="$(repo_root "$0")" || exit 9
+cd "$ROOT" || exit 9
+mkdir -p "$OUT"
+HPO_FAST_PLAN=$(SEED="$SEED" N="$N" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os, random, sys
+sys.path.insert(0, "tools/ci")
+sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
+import closure, shards
+scripts, _ = shards.suite_scripts(open("tests/run.sh").read())
+rng, n = random.Random(int(os.environ["SEED"])), int(os.environ["N"])
+group = {s: s for s in scripts}
+if os.environ.get("SPLIT_PRODUCERS") != "1":
+    for a, b in closure.lane_edges(scripts):
+        group[b] = group[a]
+draw = {g: rng.randint(1, n) for g in sorted(set(group.values()))}
+plan = {"n": n, "s": {s: draw[group[s]] for s in scripts}}
+assert shards.check(plan), "a draw left a shard empty: pick another seed"
+print(json.dumps(plan, sort_keys=True))
+PY
+) || exit 2
+export HPO_FAST_PLAN GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF="${GOLDEN_REF:-origin/main}" RUN_PART=fast GATE_SCOPE=full
+printf '%s\n' "$HPO_FAST_PLAN" > "$OUT/plan.json"
+for k in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
+  HPO_FAST_SHARD="$k/$N" ./tests/run.sh > "$OUT/shard$k.log" 2>&1
+  echo "shard $k/$N rc=$?" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
+done
+# Every `ok`/`FAILED` progress line names a script that ran; count each script once per shard.
+grep -hoE '\] (ok|FAILED) +[^ ]+ (tests/[^ ]+)' "$OUT"/shard*.log | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c \
+  | awk '$1 > 1 {print "TWICE " $2} {print "RAN " $2}' >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
+cat "$OUT/summary.txt"
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_readers.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_readers.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a1b31ac021
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_readers.py
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""The fast-job-name readers' proof (#3902 review, R11-CI-CASE-SELECT P2, #3885).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_fast_shards_readers.py WORKTREE
+
+WORKTREE is a scratch checkout of the head under test, which this harness edits: each mutant puts
+back one reader's pre-#3902 reading of the job name (or plants the review's run.sh mutant), runs
+that reader's own self-test, and restores the file. EXPECTED RESULT: the baseline line reads green
+for every self-test, and every mutant line reads KILLED: the check the fix added goes red without
+the fix. A SURVIVED line is a check that does not pin its reader.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SELF = {
+    "prelude": ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/prelude.py", "--self-test"],
+    "gate": ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/gate.py", "--self-test"],
+    "sweep": ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/sweep.py", "--self-test"],
+    "shards": ["python3", "-I", "tools/ci/shards.py", "--self-test"],
+    "probe": ["python3", "tools/audit/seat/probe_bridge.py", "--self-test"],
+    "replan": ["python3", "-I", "tools/plan/replan.py", "--self-test"],
+}
+MUTANTS = [
+    ("review: run.sh compares the shard count, not the index", "shards", "tests/run.sh",
+     '[ "$owner" != "${FAST_SHARD%/*}" ]', '[ "$owner" != "${FAST_SHARD#*/}" ]'),
+    ("prelude: the fast lane owes the unsharded name only", "prelude", "tools/ci/prelude.py",
+     'for k in (shards.owed_fast(listed) if (u, n) == ("tests", shards.FAST) else [f"{u} / {n}"])]',
+     'for k in [f"{u} / {n}"]]'),
+    ("gate.status: the listed shards only, whatever their count", "gate", "tools/ci/gate.py",
+     'for m in (shards.owed_fast(jobs) if n == f"tests / {FAST}" else [n])]',
+     'for m in ((sorted(x for x in jobs if x.startswith(f"tests / {FAST[:-1]}, ")) or [n]) '
+     'if n == f"tests / {FAST}" else [n])]'),
+    ("sweep.code_red: the required names only", "sweep", "tools/ci/sweep.py",
+     '(n in REQUIRED["no-pr"] or shards.is_fast(n))', 'n in REQUIRED["no-pr"]'),
+    ("probe_bridge: the unsharded lane only", "probe", "tools/audit/seat/probe_bridge.py",
+     'if not (name.startswith("tests / ") and shards.is_fast(name)) or', 'if name != LANE or'),
+    ("replan: the shards are not folded", "replan", "tools/plan/replan.py",
+     "    return _fold_fast(best)\n",
+     '    return {n: {k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != "finished"} for n, r in best.items()}\n'),
+    ("census: a reader dropped from READERS", "shards", "tools/ci/shards.py",
+     '    "tools/plan/replan.py": "sharded",\n', ""),
+]
+
+
+def green(root: Path, key: str) -> bool:
+    r = subprocess.run(SELF[key], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=1800)
+    return r.returncode == 0
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    if len(argv) != 1:
+        print(__doc__.split("\n\n")[1], file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    root = Path(argv[0]).resolve()
+    base = {k: green(root, k) for k in sorted({m[1] for m in MUTANTS})}
+    print("BASELINE " + " ".join(f"{k}={'green' if v else 'RED'}" for k, v in base.items()))
+    if not all(base.values()):
+        return 1
+    survived = 0
+    for name, key, rel, old, new in MUTANTS:
+        p = root / rel
+        text = p.read_text()
+        if text.count(old) != 1:
+            print(f"UNPLANTED {name}: the site occurs {text.count(old)} times in {rel}")
+            survived += 1
+            continue
+        p.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
+        try:
+            killed = not green(root, key)
+        finally:
+            p.write_text(text)
+        survived += not killed
+        print(f"{'KILLED  ' if killed else 'SURVIVED'} {name}")
+    print(f"READERS MUTANTS: {len(MUTANTS) - survived} of {len(MUTANTS)} killed")
+    return 1 if survived else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

                 runs.start_count(space + x, floor, planner.charge_runs.running))

             if watch.builds:
                 watch.builds[-1]["verdicts"].append((np.array(candidate), got))
             return got
@@ -245,7 +246,7 @@ def hysteresis() -> int:
                     continue
                 lost = 0
